scope: Independent final read-only artwork review, boot measurement clarification, and selected/raw inventory audit. This report writes no artwork and does not claim a fresh browser playback. Root has separate prior four-mode playback evidence.

visual_findings.NE02_v2: The head, neck, waist and robe retain the same body scale as NE01/03. The screen-left boot is swinging with its sole visible and the screen-right boot supports; distinct boot depths are visually coherent. No blank crop, residual matte or isolated edge flecks seen.
visual_findings.NE13_v4: The screen-left boot supports while the screen-right boot rolls/sways through. The upper-body position is consistent with NE12/14; it no longer reads as a sudden body sink. The two spirits, scroll, yin-yang pendant, tassels and brush remain present.
visual_findings.NE12_13_14: The legs exchange support within the second half-cycle and move into the next recovery phase. There is ordinary pose-dependent cloth and topknot motion; no visually blocking body-scale jump found in the static sequence.
visual_findings.seam15_16_01_02: The back-facing camera, head/torso scale and hand-held props remain consistent. The left boot stays in the matching swing progression across the cycle boundary; no extra leg, pose inversion or abrupt silhouette reset observed.
visual_findings.measurement_boundary: Whole visible-alpha max_y=942 is a canvas placement measurement, not proof that every support-boot contact pixel is y942. NE13 support boot is y937 while the other swinging toe reaches y942. This 5-pixel separation is accepted here as minor oblique-view foot projection within a roughly 800-pixel character and coherent adjacent poses. It must remain disclosed; do not rename it exact support-foot locking. NE02 also has a 6-pixel difference between its two differently posed boots.
visual_findings.review_limit: Visual acceptance above is a judgement from actually viewed static deep/light contacts, seam and native-size final PNGs. Numeric measurements only qualify the anchor claim; they do not substitute for visual judgement or prove physical ground contact.
